claims.statement: One UseFramework instance is one bounded context: the constructor creates per-instance state (logger name/observability identity, ContextMixin storage, a FrameworkContainer, dynamic_dep_registry with its DependencyLocator, three error-handler lists, and a MiddlewarePipeline) rather than module globals, so two instances in one process do not share buses or registries.

The framework has exactly three bus classes over the abstract Bus: FeatureBus owns feature_registry and spans its executions with layer "feature"; ApplicationServiceBus owns app_service_registry and spans with "application_service"; FrameworkBus is a facade that owns no registry and never executes a handler itself.

Both registries are keyed by the input DTO class __name__ (registration and lookup alike), and routing is decided purely by membership: FrameworkBus re-checks at call time that the name is not in both registries (raising DTOAlreadyRegistered) before delegating to feature_bus, then app_service_bus, and raising UnknownDTOToExecute when the name is in neither.

Container provider scoping determines the build lifecycle: feature_bus and app_service_bus are providers.Singleton while framework_bus is providers.Factory, so a second build_root_bus() produces a new facade over the same sub-bus instances and registries; ApplicationService instances are built with framework_container.feature_bus, so an ApplicationService delegates to the very same FeatureBus the facade holds.

build_root_bus() is the single wiring point that pushes dynamic dependencies onto every already-registered handler, attaches the three error handlers to their buses, materialises self.bus from the container, binds every handler instance to the framework so self.context resolves to the live context, copies the log flags onto facade and sub-buses, publishes the dto_registry onto the facade for introspection, and starts observability.

One Observability object exists per UseFramework instance and must reach all three buses unchanged; it is the only object the buses talk to, which is why no other module in the package imports opentelemetry or sentry_sdk — per-bus backend providers and error clients are kept outside the buses in observability/registry.py so a second build reuses them.

Error handling is three independent handler chains (global, feature, app-service) on the UseFramework instance; each is folded by build_error_handler_chain so that first-registered runs first and a re-raise delegates to the next handler, and each is pushed onto a single handle_error callable of the matching bus.

Context storage belongs to the instance through ContextMixin, which owns only the shared dict plus the ContextVar overlay; build_root_bus binds every registered Feature and ApplicationService to that binder, and handlers read the live dict through ContextConsumer.context with a private fallback dict when unbound.

The runtime public surface is exactly the eight names re-exported by sincpro_framework/__init__.py: UseFramework, Feature, ApplicationService, DataTransferObject, TypeDTO, TypeDTOResponse, Middleware and logger. Everything else — ioc.py, bus.py, deps.py, exceptions.py, error_handler.py, sincpro_conf.py, and the context/, observability/, introspection/, entrypoints/, aio/ and ddd/ packages — is internal and must be imported explicitly.

The shipped typing contract is the empty sincpro_framework/py.typed marker plus hand-written stub files for use_bus, bus, sincpro_abstractions, aio/bus and context/framework_context; the stubs are what make UseFramework[DependencyContextType] and the return_type argument meaningful to a type checker, and they are enforced by running pyright over the static examples in tests/typing_and_linter/typing_cases and by make lint over sincpro_framework and tests.

Host dependencies are optional extras, not required imports: fastmcp, starlette/uvicorn, the OpenTelemetry SDKs and sentry-sdk are declared as extras in pyproject.toml, and the entrypoint hosts raise a message naming the missing extra instead of failing at import time.

Observability exposes exactly two entry points for consumers: Observability, which belongs to one UseFramework and is the only object the buses talk to, and the process singleton in observability/api.py, which instruments the transport around those buses without borrowing a bus's identity.

Introspection is the single place that knows the bus's internal shape (feature_registry, app_service_registry, dto_registry) and how to describe a registered handler; it refuses an unbuilt framework with ValueError, and the entrypoints layer builds on that same metadata rather than reaching into FrameworkBus itself.

The driving adapters share one contract: Catalog projects a built instance into PackedFeatureOrAppService entries (building the root bus if needed), and both the MCP host (build_mcp_server) and the JSON-RPC host (RpcGateway) consume that same catalog; Layer in entrypoints/const.py reuses the bus's own two-registry vocabulary as "features" and "app_services".

FrameworkContainer declares an injected_dependencies providers.Dict that is never read anywhere in the package; the real dependency path is UseFramework calling add_attributes(**dynamic_dep_registry) on every registered Feature and ApplicationService at build time, plus the read-only DependencyLocator exposed as framework.deps.

Configuration and logging are attached at import time: sincpro_conf builds the settings object eagerly from a YAML file (defaulting to the packaged conf/sincpro_framework_conf.yml, overridable via SINCPRO_FRAMEWORK_CONFIG_FILE) with $ENV:-prefixed values resolved from the environment, and sincpro_logger configures global logging on import before creating the named framework logger.

docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md is the authoritative hand-written design document for patterns and diagrams and is not replaced by the wiki, but its prose is stale in places: its version footer is stamped v2.4.1 while pyproject.toml declares version 4.0.0, and docs/README.md links to a docs/architecture/README.md that does not exist in the repository.

The abstract Bus defines two cross-thread handles that all three concrete buses inherit: thread_context() returning a ThreadContextBus bound to a captured contextvars snapshot, and get_async_bus() returning a reusable AsyncBus — so which bus a handle is taken from determines which layer the handed-off execution runs through.

The dependency-injection path has two enforced failure semantics: UseFramework.add_dependency raises DependencyAlreadyRegistered rather than overwriting an existing name, and DependencyLocator (the object behind framework.deps) is read-only — a missing name raises DependencyNotRegistered, an AttributeError subclass, and __setattr__/__delattr__ are blocked.

Registration invariants are enforced at different boundaries, which determines when a violation surfaces: a duplicate DTO name within one registry is caught at decoration time (ioc._register_service) and again in the bus register_* methods; a name present in both registries is caught at FrameworkBus construction and re-checked on every execute call; an unregistered name reaches only the per-call UnknownDTOToExecute; and SincproFrameworkNotBuilt is raised only when bus is still None after the lazy build in __call__.

Free-threading is not implemented or targeted in this codebase: on a python3.14t interpreter, importing dependency_injector causes CPython to re-enable the GIL process-wide and print a RuntimeWarning, and grpcio (a transitive dependency of the OTLP gRPC exporter) does the same as soon as that exporter is used; regular GIL builds of 3.12/3.13/3.14 are unaffected. Both notes live next to the import in ioc.py and in the pyproject.toml dependency comment block rather than in the hand-written docs.

The hand-written ARCHITECTURE.md is stale on dependencies as well as version: its core-dependency block lists dependency-injector ^4.46.0, pydantic ^2.9.2 and sincpro-log ^1.0.1, while pyproject.toml declares ^4.49.1, ^2.13.5 and ^1.2.1.
